- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast low by 5–10%.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward sentiment spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to peak values.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model fails to adjust downward; apply a mean-reversion bias correction toward prior 5–7 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon; reduce first 5–7 days by 3–5% to align with observed decay.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1 → -1 → +1), model exhibits oscillation bias; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 3-day moving average.
